ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r7.claim: Jacob asks what happened to them and their sheep, and where Joseph is; they answer that the matter is worse.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r7.anchor: قال ما لكم يا بني هل أصابكم في غنمكم شي قالوا الأمر أعظم قال فما هو وأين يوسف

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r8.claim: Nastabiq means to compete in racing or archery, each seeking to win.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r8.anchor: إنا ذهبنا نستبق} أو الرمي يقال استبق الرجلان وتسابقا إذا عارضا في السبق

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r9.claim: Matāʿ means useful goods such as clothing and provisions; in 12:65 it means food containers.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r9.anchor: عند متاعنا أي : ما نتمع به من الثياب والأزواد وغيرهما فإن المتاع في اللغة كل ما انتفع به

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r10.claim: They claim the wolf ate Joseph immediately after they left him, without the interval normally needed for supervision.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r10.anchor: {فأكله الذئب} عقيب ذلك من غير مضي زمان يعتاد فيه التفقد والتعهد

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r11.claim: They say Jacob will not believe them even if he regards them as truthful because of his intense love for Joseph and distrust of them.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r11.anchor: وما أنت بمؤمن لنا بمصدق لنا في مقالتنا ولو كنا عندك في اعتقادك صادقين

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r12.claim: Truth reports something as it is and falsehood reports otherwise; verbal affirmation declares a speaker truthful, while inner affirmation accepts it.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r12.anchor: والصدق هو الإخبار عن الشيء على ما هو به والكذب لا على ما هو به والتصديق باللسان

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#2/r1.claim: نستبق means competing in archery; سبق can refer to the stake or prize.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#2/r1.anchor: ننتضل، يسابق بعضنا بعضا في الرمي

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#2/r2.claim: وما أنت بمؤمن لنا means you do not believe or trust us.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r1.claim: The brothers say they left Joseph by their belongings while racing and that a wolf ate him.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r1.anchor: عن السدى قال : ثم اقبلوا إلى ابيهم عشاء يبكون ، فلما سمع اصواتهم فزع وقال : يا بني مالكم ؟

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r2.claim: They mean Jacob will not believe them, even if they are truthful.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r2.anchor: وبه ، عن السدى قوله : وما انت بمؤمن لنا قال : وما انت بمصدق لنا ، ولو كنا صادقين .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r3.claim: The phrase means Jacob would not believe them even if they were truthful.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110#2/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق : وما انت بمؤمن لنا اي : ما انت بمصدقنا ولو كنا صادقين وان كنا قد صدقنا .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r4.claim: Nastabiq means running on foot in competition; al-Zajjaj also gives archery as a kind of contest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r4.anchor: ونستبق معناه: على الأقدام أي نجري غلابا، وقيل: بالرمي أي ننتصل.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r5.claim: Mā anta bi-muʾmin means you do not believe us; the phrase even if we are truthful may mean they are asserting that they speak truth, continuing their lie.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r5.anchor: وقولهم: وما أنت بمؤمن أي بمصدق ومعنى الكلام: أي لو كنا موصوفين بالصدق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r6.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r6.claim: A different explanation is that Jacob would not believe them in this particular disaster even if he had trusted their earlier statements, given grief, hardship, and his prior suspicion; the author finds an analogy offered by al-Rummani unsound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r6.anchor:
وقيل:
المعنى: ولو كنت تعتقد ذلك فينا في جميع أقوالنا قديما لما صدقتنا في هذه النازلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r7.speaker: المبرد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r7.claim: Al-Mubarrad reads the phrase as even if we are truthful, a continuation of the brothers’ assertion; the author says the analogy with awlaw kunnākārihīn is questionable and corrects al-Rummani’s account of their accusation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r7.anchor: القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا قول ذكره الزجاج وغيره، ويحتمل أن يكون قولهم: ولو كنا صادقين،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Qutayba explain nastabiq as competing in archery.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r1.anchor: ننتضل قاله ابن عباس وابن قتيبة قال والمعنى يسابق بعضنا بعضا في الرمي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the brothers went out racing on foot.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r4.claim: Matāʿ means their clothes; muʾmin means one who believes their claim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r4.anchor: أي ثيابنا ( وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ) أي يمصدق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq takes “even if we were truthful” to mean even if what they said were true.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r5.anchor: أن المعنى وإن كنا قد صدقنا قاله ابن إسحاق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says that even if they were normally trustworthy, Jacob would still suspect them about Joseph because he loved him and think they had lied.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191#2/r6.anchor: لو كنا عندك من أهل الصدق لا تهمتنا في يوسف لمحبتك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375/r1.claim: After abandoning Joseph in the well, his brothers return to Jacob at night pretending grief and explain that they left him with their belongings while they raced and a wolf ate him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375/r1.anchor: رجعوا إلى أبيهم في ظلمة الليل يبكون، ويظهرون الأسف والجزع على يوسف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375/r2.claim: Their claim that Jacob would not believe them even if truthful is calculated tact: they acknowledge his suspicion was understandable because he had warned them about the wolf and the outcome sounds unlikely.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375/r2.anchor: تلطف عظيم في تقرير ما يحاولونه، يقولون: ونحن نعلم أنك لا تصدقنا

JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r7.claim: Istibāq is racing to get ahead; the text surveys race stakes and reports that foot races and wrestling may be allowed, with disagreement over compensation and whether a contract binds.
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r7.anchor: يجوز بعوض وغير عوض، ولأصحاب الشافعي فيه وجهان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r4.claim: Nastabiqu means they raced; iftiʿāl and tafāʿul may share meaning, and they could race by running or archery.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r4.anchor: أي نتسابق ، والافتعال والتفاعل يشتركان كالانتضال والتناضل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r5.claim: They say Jacob will not believe even if they are truthful because of his intense love for Joseph and distrust of them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r5.anchor: ولو كنا عندك من أهل الصدق والثقة ، لشدة محبتك ليوسف ، فكيف وأنت سيء الظن بنا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r1.claim: Nastabiq derives from the form iftiʿāl of sabāq; it may mean competing in archery.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r1.anchor: وهو نفتعل من السباق وفيه أربعة أوجه : أحدها : معناه ننتصل , من السباق في الرمي , قاله الزجاج

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r2.speaker: الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r2.claim: The brothers may mean that they raced each other on foot.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r2.anchor: أنهم أرادوا السبق بالسعي على أقدامهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r3.claim: Alternatively, they competed in the work they were doing, such as herding or gathering firewood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r3.anchor: أنهم عنوا استباقهم في العمل الذي تشاغلوا به من الرعي والاحتطاب

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r4.claim: Alternatively, they competed in hunting and catching game.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r4.anchor: أي نتصيد وأنهم يستبقون على اقتناص الصيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r5.claim: Leaving Joseph by their belongings may have expressed concern for him or kept watch over their baggage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r5.anchor: يحتمل أن يعنوا بتركه عند متاعهم إظهار الشفقة عليه , ويحتمل أن يعنوا حفظ رحالهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r6.claim: The brothers exploited Jacob's earlier fear of a wolf when they claimed that the wolf had eaten Joseph.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r6.anchor: لما سمعوا أباهم يقول : وأخاف أن يأكله الذئب أخذوا ذلك من فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r7.claim: Muʾmin here means one who believes or accepts their account.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r7.anchor: وما أنت بمؤمن لنا } أي بمصدق لنا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r8.claim: Their qualification “even if we were truthful” means that even if they were honest people Jacob would not believe them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r8.anchor: أنه لم يكن ذلك منهم تشكيكا لأبيهم في صدقهم وإنما عنوا : ولو كنا أهل صدق ما صدقتنا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r9.speaker: ابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r9.claim: The phrase may mean “even though we have told the truth.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r9.anchor: معناه وإن كنا قد صدقنا , قاله ابن إسحاق

MUQATIL:12:16-18/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r1.claim: Joseph’s brothers come to Jacob at the evening prayer, claiming they went hunting and left Joseph guarding their belongings; the wolf ate him, they say, and Jacob will not believe them even if truthful.
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r1.anchor: { وجآءوا أباهم } يعقوب { عشآء يبكون } [آية: 16] صلاة العتمة.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#3/r1.claim: Nastabiqū may mean racing on foot or competing in archery; the derived forms iftiʿāl and tafāʿul can overlap, as in throwing/competing to throw.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#3/r1.anchor: أى نتسابق العدو أو فى الرمى والافتعال والتفاعل يشتركان كالارتماء والترامى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#3/r2.claim: They say Jacob will not believe their story even if they speak truth, because he loves Joseph intensely and distrusts the brothers.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ ولو كنا صادقين ﴾ ولو كنا عندك من أهل الصدق والثقة لشدة محبتك ليوسف

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r1.claim: “At night” is a temporal circumstance; the brothers came after dark to make their excuse easier. A saying advises not seeking favors at night, when shame shows in the eyes, or trying to excuse a daytime wrong, when speech falters.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r1.anchor: أي ليلا، وهو ظرف يكون في موضع الحال

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r2.claim: A report tells that when Jacob heard them crying he asked what had happened and where Joseph was; they answered that they had raced off and the wolf ate him, after which he cried out and asked for the shirt.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r2.anchor: فروي أن يعقوب عليه السلام لما سمع بكاءهم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r3.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r3.claim: Al-Suddi and Ibn Hibban say Jacob collapsed unconscious at the claim that a wolf ate Joseph; Judah found no sign of life, lamented that they had lost their brother and killed their father, and Jacob woke at dawn with Reuben supporting him before Judah repeated their story.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r3.anchor: وقال السدي وابن حبان: إنه لما قالوا

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r4.speaker: وهب
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r4.claim: Wahb recounts Judah checking Jacob's breathing and pulse, then rebuking himself and his brothers for losing Joseph and nearly causing their father's death.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r4.anchor: قال وهب: ولقد وضع يهوذا يده

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r5.claim: Tears do not prove the truth of what someone says, since a person may manufacture tears, though some people can do this and others cannot.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r5.anchor: قال علماؤنا: هذه الآية دليل على أن بكاء المرء

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r6.claim: A saying attributed to a sage says that mingled tears on cheeks reveal who is weeping and who is pretending.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17/r6.anchor: إذا اشتبكت دموع في خدود تبين من بكى ممن تباكى

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r1.claim: “Nastabiq” is a derived form meaning “we race”; the alternative “nintadil” in ʿAbd Allah's reading means they engaged in archery, a type of competition.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r1.anchor: نفتعل، من المسابقة. وقيل: أي ننتضل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls archery a form of competition; al-Azhari distinguishes contests of arrows from horse races, with “competition” encompassing both.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r2.anchor: قاله الزجاج. وقال الأزهري: النضال في السهام

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r3.speaker: أبو نصر القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r3.claim: Al-Qushayri says the brothers might have been competing at archery, on horseback, or on foot; running trains the body for chasing an enemy and protecting sheep from a wolf.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r3.anchor: قال القشيري أبو نصر: «نستبق» أي في الرمي

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r4.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi and Ibn Hibban understand that the brothers ran hard to see which of them was fastest.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi calls racing a legitimate and excellent practice and aid to warfare; the Prophet raced on foot and with horses, and raced ʿAʾisha, first winning and later—when older—losing, then saying “this for that.”
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن العربي: المسابقة شرعة في الشريعة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r6.claim: Qurtubi adds that Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ raced a man returning from Dhu Qarad to Medina and won; Muslim transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r6.anchor: قلت: وسابق سلمة بن الأكوع رجلا

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r7.claim: Malik transmits that the Prophet raced trained horses from al-Hafya to Thaniyyat al-Wadaʿ and untrained horses from the latter place to the mosque of Banu Zurayq; Ibn ʿUmar joined the races.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r7.anchor: روى مالك عن نافع عن ابن عمر: أن رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r8.claim: Qurtubi derives three conditions from this sound report: the distance must be known, horses comparable in condition, and trained horses cannot race untrained horses over the same distance; the horses for this Sunnah are those prepared to fight enemies, not Muslims in civil strife.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r8.anchor: وهذا الحديث مع صحته في هذا الباب تضمن ثلاثة شروط

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r9.claim: A Muslim report from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr mentions travelers with the Prophet practicing archery during a stop.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#2/r9.anchor: فمنا من يصلح خباءه، ومنا من ينتضل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r1.claim: Muslims agree that prize wagers are allowed only in archery, camels, and horses; al-Shafiʿi regards wagering in other contests as gambling.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r1.anchor: أجمع المسلمون على أن السبق لا يجوز على وجه الرهان

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r2.claim: The extra “or wing” in Abu al-Bakhtari's version of the hadith was fabricated for the caliph al-Rashid, so scholars rejected this narrator and his other fabrications.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r2.anchor: وقد زاد أبو البختري القاضي في حديث الخف والحافر والنصل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r3.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r3.claim: Malik allows prizes only for horses and archery because they strengthen war effort, and prefers horse racing; the hadith's apparent scope also includes camels.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r3.anchor: وقد روي عن مالك أنه قال: لا سبق إلا في الخيل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r4.claim: Some jurists allow wagering only on horses, the customary Arab race; ʿAtaʾ reportedly allows it in any contest, but Qurtubi says such a general reading would license gambling, which is agreed to be forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r4.anchor: وقد منع بعض العلماء الرهان في كل شيء إلا في الخيل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r5.claim: Horse and camel races require a known finish and distance; archery also requires a known target, number of rounds, and agreed hit criterion such as piercing through or another specified strike.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r5.anchor: لا يجوز السبق في الخيل والإبل إلا في غاية معلومة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r6.claim: The first permitted prize arrangement is a ruler or other donor voluntarily offering a known award to the winner; the second is a one-sided stake, which the winner may take and the loser does not reclaim, with no scholarly disagreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r6.anchor: سبق يعطيه الوالي أو الرجل غير الوالي من ماله متطوعا

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r7.claim: When both racers stake money for the winner, the arrangement is only permitted with a third entrant who could beat either: if the entrant wins, he takes both stakes; if either racer wins, that racer takes both, and the entrant neither pays nor receives.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r7.anchor: وهذا الوجه لا يجوز حتى يدخلا بينهما محللا لا يأمنا

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r8.speaker: أبو علي بن خيران
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r8.claim: Abu ʿAli ibn Khayran says the third, qualifying horse's racing ability must be unknown; he is called a muhallil because his participation makes the wager lawful.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r8.anchor: وقال أبو علي بن خيران من أصحاب الشافعي : وحكم الفرس المحلل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r9.claim: Scholars agree that when both racers stipulate that the winner takes the other's stake and there is no qualifying third entrant, the arrangement is gambling and forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r9.anchor: واتفق العلماء على أنه إن لم يكن بينهما محلل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r10.claim: Bukhari reports that the Prophet's she-camel al-ʿAdba was rarely beaten until a Bedouin's mount outran her; when Muslims were saddened, the Prophet said God lowers whatever worldly thing rises.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r10.anchor: وروى البخاري عن أنس قال: كان للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ناقة تسمى العضباء

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r11.claim: Al-Nasaʾi reports Abu Hurayra’s Prophetic hadith that a prize is permitted only for arrows, camel racing, or horse racing; jurists of the Hijaz and Iraq rely on it.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#3/r11.anchor: لا سبق إلا في نصل أو خف أو حافر

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r1.claim: A Prophetic report says a horse inserted between two is not gambling if its ability to beat them is uncertain, but is gambling if it is certain to lose; Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib similarly permits a horse wager with a qualifying entrant, as do al-Shafiʿi and most scholars.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r1.anchor: من أدخل فرسا بين فرسين وهو لا يأمن أن يسبق فليس بقمار

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r2.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r2.claim: Malik first said a qualifying entrant is unnecessary and did not follow Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, but later required one; Qurtubi calls Malik's latter view the better one.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r2.anchor: واختلف في ذلك قول مالك فقال مرة لا يجب المحلل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r3.claim: ʿUmar says only a horse's owner should ride it in a race; Qurtubi also says the rider should be an adult, though an owner riding is preferable.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r3.anchor: وقد روي عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أنه قال: لا يركب الخيل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r4.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r4.claim: Al-Shafiʿi defines the minimum lead in racing as the muzzle or part of it passing, or the hindquarters or part; the same rule applies to archers, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan agrees.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r4.anchor: وقال الشافعي: وأقل السبق أن يسبق بالهادي

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r5.claim: A report says the Prophet raced Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, winning himself while Abu Bakr came second and ʿUmar third; “Abu Bakr came second” means his horse's head reached the rear of the Prophet's horse.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r5.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سابق أبا بكر وعمر

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r6.claim: The brothers left Joseph guarding their clothes, baggage, and belongings.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r6.anchor: أي عند ثيابنا وأقمشتنا حارسا لها.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r7.claim: They reused Jacob's expressed fear that a wolf might eat Joseph as the basis for their lie.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r7.anchor: لما سمعوا أباهم يقول: «وأخاف أن يأكله الذئب»

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r8.claim: Here “believe us” means “believe what we say.”
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r8.anchor: { ومآ أنت بمؤمن لنا } أي بمصدق.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r9.claim: Their father did not believe them because their accusation was strong and evidence contradicted it.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r9.anchor: ولم يصدقهم يعقوب لما ظهر له منهم من قوة التهمة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad and Ibn Ishaq take “wa-law kunna” to mean “even if we were” or “even though we were.”
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r10.anchor: أي وإن كنا قاله المبرد وابن إسحق.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r11.claim: Al-Tabari, al-Zajjaj, and others offer another interpretation: the brothers thought Jacob would doubt them even if they had been known as trustworthy, because of his intense love for Joseph.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:17#4/r11.anchor: لشدة محبتك في يوسف قال معناه الطبري والزجاج وغيرهما.

RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says istibāq means competing in archery; a prophetic report permits prize contests only in camel racing, archery, or horse racing, and archery competition tests distance.
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج : يسابق بعضهم بعضا في الرمي ، ومنه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( لا سبق إلا في خف أو نصل أو حافر )

RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r5.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r5.claim: Al-Suddī and Muqātil instead explain “we were competing” as running to see who was fastest.
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني : في تفسير الاستباق ما قاله السدي ومقاتل : { ذهبنا نستبق } نشتد ونعدو ليتبين أينا أسرع عدوا

RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r6.claim: Adult brothers could race to train their running, useful in fighting enemies or defending against a wolf that snatched a sheep.
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r6.anchor: كانوا يجربون بذلك أنفسهم ويدربونها على العدو ولأنه كالآلة لهم في محاربة العدو

RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r7.claim: Some say the wolf ate Joseph and others that the brothers exposed the baggage to a wolf; the author favors the first reading.
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r7.anchor: وقوله : { فأكله الذئب } قيل أكل الذئب يوسف وقيل عرضوا وأرادوا أكل الذئب المتاع ، والوجه هو الأول

RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r8.claim: “You will not believe us” does not mean Jacob rejects someone he knows is truthful; they mean his love for Joseph makes him suspect them, or that they have shown no evidence of truth.
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r8.anchor: ليس المعنى أن يعقوب عليه السلام لا يصدق من يعلم أنه صادق ، بل المعنى لو كنا عندك من أهل الثقة والصدق لاتهمتنا

RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r1.claim: The brothers stained the shirt with a kid's blood to make the wolf story seem credible; al-Qāḍī suggests they had stripped Joseph before putting him in the well to prepare this deception.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r1.anchor: إنما جاؤا بهذا القميص الملطخ بالدم ليوهم كونهم صادقين في مقالتهم

RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r2.claim: Al-Qāḍī reasons that if the shirt had been torn as well as bloodied the lie would be more convincing; its intact state revealed the brothers' falsehood to Jacob.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r2.anchor: فلما شاهد يعقوب القميص صحيحا علم كذبهم

RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r3.claim: The phrase “they came upon his shirt with blood” means the blood was over the shirt, as one may say they came on their camels with loads.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r3.anchor: قوله : { وجاءوا على قميصه } أي وجاؤا فوق قميصه بدم كما يقال : جاؤا على جمالهم بأحمال

RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r4.speaker: الفراء والمبرد والزجاج وابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r4.claim: The grammarians read dam kadhib as blood in which they lied: a verbal noun is used for the object or agent, as in “spilled water,” “a just man,” and related Qur'anic expressions.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r4.anchor: قال أصحاب العربية وهم الفراء والمبرد والزجاج وابن الأنباري { بدم كذب } أي مكذوب فيه

RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r5.speaker: الشعبي
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says Joseph's story is all in his shirt: his brothers removed it and bloodied it, a witness later examines whether it was torn from the front, and the shirt eventually restores Jacob's sight.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82/r5.anchor: قال الشعبي : قصة يوسف كلها في قميصه ، وذلك لأنهم لما ألقوه في الجب نزعوا قميصه

SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r1.claim: نستبق means race one another; افتعال and تفاعل can share senses, as in competing in archery or throwing.
SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r1.anchor: نستبق }: نتسابق، والافتعال والتفاعل يشتركان نحو قولهم: ننتضل ونتناضل

SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r2.claim: نستبق is circumstantial, and تركنا is another circumstantial clause with قد understood by some grammarians.
SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r2.anchor: و " نستبق " في محل نصب على الحال. و " تركنا " حال من " نستبق " و " قد " معه مضمرة عند بعضهم

SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r3.claim: ولو كنا صادقين is a circumstantial clause: their father would not believe them even if they were truthful because he suspected their hatred of Joseph.
SAMIN-DURR:12:17/r3.anchor: أي: ما أنت مصدقا لنا في كل حال حتى في حال صدقنا لما غلب على ظنك

STUDYQURAN:12:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r3.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r3.claim: When the brothers said the sheep were unharmed, Jacob asked what had happened and where Joseph was.
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r3.anchor: “What happened to you then, and where is Joseph?” (Bg)

STUDYQURAN:12:16/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r4.claim: The brothers claim they raced to train for fighting enemies and wolves that had been taking their sheep.
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r4.anchor: they went racing with one another in order to train themselves so that they could combat enemies and the wolf

STUDYQURAN:12:16/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r5.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r5.claim: “Their things” means the brothers' garments and clothes.
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r5.anchor: they had left Joseph with their things, namely, their garments and clothes (Bg)

STUDYQURAN:12:16/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r6.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r6.claim: Upon hearing Joseph was dead, Jacob fainted; the brothers poured water on him, and he remained unconscious until the next morning.
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r6.anchor: Jacob fainted, and the brothers poured water over him to wake him up. Yet he remained unconscious until early the next morning (Q)

STUDYQURAN:12:16/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r7.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r7.claim: The brothers say Jacob would not believe them even if truthful because they felt he had a bad opinion of them.
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r7.anchor: they felt Jacob had a bad opinion of them (Bḍ)

STUDYQURAN:12:16/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r8.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r8.claim: From Jacob's perspective, suspicion of his sons already made their story unbelievable; Genesis instead says he believed their account.
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r8.anchor: From Jacob’s perspective, he could not believe them, because he was suspicious of them to begin with (R)

STUDYQURAN:12:16/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r9.claim: The brothers' complaint recalls their earlier question about Jacob's distrust and foreshadows their later truthful report that he still disbelieves, partly because of their actions.
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r9.anchor: This mistrust of the brothers foreshadows an incident later in this sūrah in which the brothers return to Jacob with some news about which they were actually being truthful

TAB-FULL:v13p34/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p34/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p34/r2.claim: The word نستبق is explained as competing in a race or archery contest.
TAB-FULL:v13p34/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن معنى قوله: {نستبق} [يوسف: 17] ننتضل من السباق

TAB-FULL:v13p34#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p34#2/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p34#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi glosses مؤمن as believing or crediting the brothers; al-Tabari rejects readings that they confess they are liars or say their father would disbelieve truthful people, taking it to mean he distrusts them.
TAB-FULL:v13p34#2/r1.anchor: عن أسباط، عن السدي، " {وما أنت بمؤمن لنا} [يوسف: 17] قال: بمصدق لنا.

TAB-FULL:v13p34#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p34#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p34#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari rejects readings that the brothers confess they are liars or say their father would disbelieve even truthful people; it means he distrusts and suspects them, even if truthful.
TAB-FULL:v13p34#2/r2.anchor: قيل: ليس معنى ذلك بواحد منهما، وإنما معنى ذلك: وما أنت بمصدق لنا ولو كنا من أهل الصدق الذين لا يتهمون

ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r4.claim: نستبق means competing with one another; it is also explained as competing in archery, ننتضل.

ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r5.claim: مؤمن لنا means ‘believing us’ or ‘accepting our account.’
ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r5.anchor:
(فأكله الذئب وما أنت بمؤمن لنا)
أي بمصدق لنا.

ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r6.claim: The brothers do not mean Jacob would reject something he knew true, which would be impossible to ascribe to a prophet; they mean his love for Joseph would make him suspect their account.
ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r6.anchor: ليس يريدون أن يعقوب - عليه السلام - لا يصدق من يعلم أنه صادق، هذا محال، لا يوصف الأنبياء بذلك،

TABATABAI:12:17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17/r1.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:12:17/r1.claim: Al-Raghib defines sabq as preceding in movement and istibaq as racing or competing.
TABATABAI:12:17/r1.anchor: أصل السبق التقدم في السير نحو { والسابقات سبقا } والاستباق التسابق

TABATABAI:12:17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:12:17/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses “we went to race” as racing in running or archery, noting that the reciprocal and reflexive forms can overlap.
TABATABAI:12:17/r2.anchor: نستبق أي نتسابق، والافتعال والتفاعل يشتركان كالانتضال والتناضل

TABATABAI:12:17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17/r3.speaker: صاحب المنار
TABATABAI:12:17/r3.claim: Al-Manar distinguishes istibaq as striving to get ahead from reciprocal competition, applying this to the brothers’ race and contrasting it with good deeds and the race to the door.
TABATABAI:12:17/r3.anchor: إنا ذهبنا نستبق أي ذهبنا من مكان اجتماعنا إلى السباق يتكلف كل منا أن يسبق غيره

TABATABAI:12:17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:17/r4.claim: Tabatabai rejects al-Manar’s distinction: “race for good deeds” and the race to the door also involve each party trying to get ahead, so istibaq and tasabuq coincide in use.
TABATABAI:12:17/r4.anchor: فالحق أن معنيي الاستباق والتسابق متحدان صدقا على المورد

TABATABAI:12:17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:17/r5.claim: The reflexive form emphasizes the agent’s effort to secure precedence for himself; because precedence is comparative, this effort entails racing against others.
TABATABAI:12:17/r5.anchor: وزنة " افتعل " تفيد تأكد معنى " فعل " وإمعان الفاعل في فعله وأخذه حلية لنفسه

TABATABAI:12:17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:17/r6.claim: “A believer in us” means someone who accepts their account; iman can take either the preposition li or bi, as in the verse about Lot.
TABATABAI:12:17/r6.anchor: وقوله { بمؤمن لنا } أي بمصدق لقولنا، والإيمان يتعدى باللام كما يتعدى بالباء

TABATABAI:12:17-18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r1.claim: The brothers claim they went into the open country to race, probably on foot, leaving Joseph with their belongings, where a wolf supposedly ate him.
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r1.anchor: ذهبنا إلى البيداء نتسابق في عدو أو رمي - ولعله كان في عدو

TABATABAI:12:17-18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r2.claim: Their admission that Jacob would not believe them even if truthful is an excuse formula used when one has run out of means; it indirectly signals that their account is true.
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r2.anchor: وقولهم { وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين } كلام يأتي بمثله المعتذر إذا انقطع عن الأسباب

TABRISI:12:13-18/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:13-18/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:13-18/r1.claim: The hamza in dhiʾb may be softened; al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, Abū Jaʿfar, Warsh, al-Aʿshā, and al-Yazīdī soften it in all three occurrences, while the rest articulate it. Plurals include adhuʾub, dhawāʾib, and dhuʾbān; tadhāʾabat the wind means it blew from every direction.
TABRISI:12:13-18/r1.anchor: وقراءة الكسائي وخلف وأبو جعفر وورش والأعشى واليزيدي بتخفيف الهمزة في المواضع الثلاث والباقون بالهمز

TABRISI:12:13-18/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:13-18/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:13-18/r3.claim: Istibāq means racing to find who is fastest; archery contests are permitted by consensus, horse and camel races are permitted by the author’s school, while foot races for prizes are barred by that school and al-Shāfiʿī but allowed by Abū Ḥanīfa and some of the author’s colleagues; the same dispute applies to wrestling.
TABRISI:12:13-18/r3.anchor: والاستباق افتعال من السبق واستبقا تبادرا حتى يظهر الأقوى ومنه المسابقة

TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r4.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī and al-Suddī explain “we went racing” as running on foot to see who was fastest; al-Zajjāj takes it to mean target practice, and a reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh is “we were shooting.”
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r4.anchor: أي نشتد ونعدو على الأقدام لننظر أينا أعدى وأسبق لصاحبه عن الجبائي والسدي

TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r5.claim: They left Joseph by their baggage to guard it. “You would not believe us even if we were truthful” has an omitted result: Jacob would still disbelieve them because he suspected their jealousy and knew their resentment.

THALABI:v5p202/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r2.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v5p202/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Jacob heard them and feared something had happened to them or their sheep, then asked where Joseph was.
THALABI:v5p202/r2.anchor: قال السدي: فلما سمع أصواتهم فزع وقال: ما لكم يا بنى؟

THALABI:v5p202/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p202/r3.claim: نستبق is glossed as throwing at one another, supported by Abdullah’s reading ننتضل; al-Suddi and Ibn Hayyan instead say ‘we raced.’
THALABI:v5p202/r3.anchor: قالوا يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق أي نترامى، دليله قول عبد الله: ننتضل

THALABI:v5p202/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p202/r4.claim: The brothers say Joseph was left with their baggage and eaten by a wolf; they expect Jacob not to believe them even if truthful because he suspects them.
THALABI:v5p202/r4.anchor: وما أنت بمؤمن مصدق لنا ولو كنا صادقين لسوء ظنك بنا

ASAD-NOTES:12:16#n17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:16#n17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:16#n17/r1.claim: Jacob disbelieved the wolf story and inferred from his sons’ envy that they had harmed Joseph, yet his hope in 12:83 shows he was not certain Joseph had died.
ASAD-NOTES:12:16#n17/r1.anchor: knowing his sons' envy of Joseph, at once realized that it was they themselves who had done grievous harm

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p44/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p44/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين؛ الزجاج؛ ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p44/r1.claim: Nastabiqu means competing in archery, supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh as nantaṣilu and the Prophetic rule that prizes are only for camels, arrows, or horses; archers compare whose arrow travels farther.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p44/r1.anchor: نتنصل في الرمي، وهذا اختيار الزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p44/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p44/r2.speaker: السدي؛ مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p44/r2.claim: They interpret it as running hard to see who is faster; though this seems childish for adult men, training their running prepared them for war and defending livestock from enemies or wolves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p44/r2.anchor: نستبق: نشتد ونعدو لنتبين أينا أسرع عدوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r1.claim: The brothers left Joseph with their clothes and belongings.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r2.speaker: عامة المفسرين؛ أصحاب المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r2.claim: Muʾmin means believing or accepting their account; the author refers to the discussion at the opening of al-Baqara.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق؛ أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r3.claim: “Even if truthful” does not accuse the prophet Jacob of disbelieving known truth; the brothers mean his suspicion and intense love of Joseph would make him distrust them regardless.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r3.anchor: ليسوا يريدون أن يعقوب لا يصدق من يعلم أنه صادق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r4.claim: They may mean they believe themselves truthful but Jacob will not be persuaded without signs; even objective truth does not establish their credibility to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p45/r4.anchor: نحن صادقون عند أنفسنا، وأنت غير مصدق لنا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r1.claim: Joseph’s brothers say they raced to see who could run fastest, left him by their clothes, and claim a wolf ate him; they expect Jacob not to believe them because he suspects them in this story.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r1.anchor: نشتد ونعدو ليتبين أينا أسرع عدوا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Istibāq means racing one another; a later verse uses it for two people running toward a door.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The word إﺳﺘﺒﺎقmeans  competing against one another in a race.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The wolf story was a weak, unintelligent excuse chosen because Jacob had already voiced that fear, and the brothers themselves doubted he would believe it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The excuse presented by the brothers was a rather poor one and did nor reflect any intelligence in it.

QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#1/r1.claim: The standard reading retains the hamza in al-dhiʾbu.

QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#2/r1.claim: A tashīl form drops the hamza and lengthens the preceding vowel, producing al-dhību.
QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#2/r1.anchor: Tashīl/hamza-dropping variant: al-dhību (hamza elided, compensatory lengthening

QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#3/r1.claim: In pause, al-dhīb ends with sukūn; connected reading uses al-dhiʾbu.
QIRAAT-ER:12:17:14#3/r1.anchor: Waqf (pause) variant: al-dhīb with sukūn; read in connected speech as al-dhiʾbu

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r4.claim: Four proposed senses of 'we were racing' are shooting arrows, racing on foot, dividing farm tasks such as watering and herding, or hunting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r4.anchor: ونستبق، أي: نترامى بالسهام، أو نتجارى على الأقدام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r5.claim: 'By our belongings' means their clothes, which they removed while competing; this and other details support Joseph's youth rather than an adolescent age.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r5.anchor: عند متاعنا أي: عند ثيابنا، وما تجردنا له حالة الاستباق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r6.claim: 'You will not believe us' can mean Jacob will not credit them even if truthful now, or will never trust them because he already suspects their hatred and scheming; their phrase could limit their claimed truth to this incident.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r6.anchor: وما أنت بمؤمن لنا أي: بمصدق لنا الآن ولو كنا صادقين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r1.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddī explains their contest as racing on foot.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes their contest to be archery; the author favors this because ʿAbd Allāh's reading says ننتضل, meaning to shoot arrows against one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r2.anchor: كما قال الزجاج أو في أعمال نتوزعها من سقي ورعي واحتطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r3.claim: Other proposed contests involve dividing tasks such as watering, herding, and gathering wood, or hunting.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r3.anchor: أو في أعمال نتوزعها من سقي ورعي واحتطاب أو في الصيد وأخذه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r4.claim: The objection that running is childish and useless is answered: it can train them to run in battle or to fend off a wolf; نستبق can mean نتسابق, and the derived forms can share the same sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r4.anchor: وثمرته التدريب في العدو لمحاربة العدو ومدافعة الذئب مثلا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r5.claim: Their claim that Joseph was left by the belongings presents him as safe among clothes and provisions, within sight and only briefly unattended, so they deny negligence in guarding him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r5.anchor: بل تركناه في مأمنا ومجمعا بمرأى منا وما فارقناه إلا ساعة يسيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r6.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r6.claim: He explains that the brothers' mention of the belongings shows they left Joseph in a safe place where threats were unlikely.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r6.anchor: فكان ما كان قاله شيخ الإسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r7.claim: He reads them as literally claiming that a wolf ate Joseph; the proposal that they hinted the wolf ate the belongings is an unwarranted departure from the plain sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r7.anchor: والظاهر أنهم لم يريدوا إلا أن الذئب أكل يوسف ولم يقصدوا بذلك تعريضا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r8.claim: They mean Jacob would not trust their account even if he regarded them as honest and reliable because of his strong love for Joseph; reading ولو كنا as an admission they were truthful would make them admit lying by contrast.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199#2/r8.anchor: أي موصوفين بالصدق والثقة لفرط محبتك فكيف وأنت سيء الظن بنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r3.claim: Nastabiq means competing in archery or shooting; al-Suddi says it means racing on foot. Their matāʿ was their clothes and belongings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r3.anchor: {قالوا يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق} أي: نترامى وننتضل، وقال السدي: نشتد على أقدامنا. {وتركنا يوسف عند متاعنا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r4.claim: Muʾmin means believing or trusting them; Jacob's apparent accusation means he suspects them because he had feared and distrusted them regarding Joseph from the outset.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r4.anchor: فإن قيل: كيف قالوا ليعقوب أنت لا تصدق الصادق؟. قيل: معناه إنك تتهمنا في هذا الأمر لأنك خفتنا في الابتداء واتهمتنا في حقه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that Jacob cannot believe them because they offer no evidence for their claim, even if they are truthful before God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا تصدقنا لأنه لا دليل لنا على صدقنا وإن كنا صادقين عند الله.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:17/r1.claim: Nastabiq means competing in running or archery; iftiʿāl and tafāʿul can both denote mutual competition, as in competing in shooting.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:17/r1.anchor: نتسابق في العدو أو في الرمي، وقد يشترك الافتعال والتفاعل كانتضال والتناضل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:17/r2.claim: The brothers claim the wolf ate Joseph and anticipate Jacob's disbelief because he suspects them and loves Joseph intensely.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:17/r2.anchor: لسوء ظنك بنا وفرط محبتك ليوسف.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r3.claim: They claim they raced, left Joseph with their belongings, and the wolf ate him; they concede Jacob will not believe them even if truthful.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r4.claim: They knew Jacob would doubt them because of his clear insight, their suspicious behavior, and the telltale signs of a lie; they had never been caught lying.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r4.anchor: لا يصدقهم من وجوه منها ما هو عليه من صحة الفراسة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r1.claim: Eating the wolf means it killed Yusuf and ate some of him; the verb can name the whole object while intending a part, as in the lion example.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r2.claim: The wolf is a pack of wolves that left no trace of Yusuf, explaining why the brothers did not say they buried him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r3.claim: The statement that Jacob will not believe them conveys that they know he will reject the story, so they were not seeking his credence.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r4.claim: The verb for believing takes li before the person believed, as in the cited examples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r4.anchor: وفعل الإيمان يعدى باللام إلى المصدق بفتح الدال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r5.claim: The waw in the brothers’ concessive clause is circumstantial, and law marks the most remote circumstance from the preceding claim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r5.anchor: وهي تفيد أنه مضمون ما بعدها هو أبعد الأحوال عن تحقق مضمون ما قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r6.claim: No deleted opposite condition is needed; concessive law and in do not imply an opposite conclusion, unlike restrictive conditionals.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r7.speaker: المعري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r7.claim: Al-Maʿarri’s line exemplifies a concessive clause without an opposite inference; Ibn ʿĀshūr also points to earlier discussions of this construction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p237/r7.anchor: وإني وإن كنت الأخير زمانه لآتت بما لم تستطعه الأوائل

MAJAZ:v1p302/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p302/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p302/r7.claim: مؤمن لنا means believing us or acknowledging that we are truthful.
MAJAZ:v1p302/r7.anchor: «وما أنت بمؤمن لنا» (17) أي بمصدق ولا مقر لنا أنه صدق

NAHHAS:v2p317/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p317/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p317/r6.claim: The phrase is explained as وإن كنا, an elliptical concession.

TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.claim: In Abu Hamza's report, Jacob's sons planned to kill Yusuf, but their eldest persuaded them to cast him into a well; they later lied that a wolf ate him, and Jacob grieved yet trusted the truthful dream God had shown him.
TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.anchor: فقال كبيرهم { لا تقتلوا يوسف } ولكن { ألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين }

SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنهلايجوزأنيقولالرجلرأيتعبد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنهلايجوزأنيقولالرجلرأيتعبد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنهلايجوزأنيقولالرجلرأيتعبد.claim: After someone names a definite person such as ʿAbd Allāh, asking منه is inappropriate because the speaker means someone identified individually; one may ask who he is or which man.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنهلايجوزأنيقولالرجلرأيتعبد.anchor: فإنما يذكر رجلا تعرفه بعينه أو رجلا أنت عنده ممن يعرفه بعينه

SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنهلايجوزأنيقولالرجلرأيتعبد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنهلايجوزأنيقولالرجلرأيتعبد.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنهلايجوزأنيقولالرجلرأيتعبد.claim: Some Arabs nevertheless ask مع منين after ذهبنا معهم or منا after رأيته when the referents are not personally known; they treat the report like رأيت رجلا.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنهلايجوزأنيقولالرجلرأيتعبد.anchor: العرب من يقال له ذهبنا معهم فيقول مع منين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.claim: For dual and masculine plural suffixes, add mīm after the dual alif or plural wāw; no further marker is added beyond two because dual is already a plural form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.anchor: فإذا عنيت مذكرين أو مؤنثين ألحقت ميما تزيد حرفا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.claim: The dual or plural suffixes -tumā and -tumū keep ḍamma on tāʾ and kāf; number and gender are marked by what follows, so the singleton vowels are no longer used.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.anchor: وتلزم التاء والكاف الضمة وتدع الحركتين اللتين كانتا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلحقالتاءوالكافاللتينل.claim: Feminine plural verb endings do not double nūn, unlike pronoun suffixes such as -tun and -kunna; doubling is avoided to prevent four or five consecutive vowels in one word.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r1.claim: Īmān fundamentally means affirmation; here the brothers say Jacob will not believe them even if they are truthful.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r2.claim: A servant is a believer by affirming; God is al-Muʾmin because He confirms what He promises and makes it real, or accepts a servant’s faith.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r2.anchor: فالعبد مؤمن، أي: مصدق محقق. والله مؤمن، أي: مصدق ما وعده ومحققه، أو قابل إيمانه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r3.claim: In ordinary speech, ما أومن بشيء مما تقول means “I do not affirm anything you say.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r3.anchor: ما أومن بشيء مما تقول؛ أي: ما أصدق بذلك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r4.claim: The Qurʾān calls prayer īmān in the verse about prayer toward Jerusalem.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r4.anchor: وقد سمى الله الصلاة - في كتابه - إيمانا؛ فقال: {وما كان الله ليضيع إيمانكم}

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r5.claim: Al-Muʾmin may also derive from security: no one is safe except one whom God has made safe.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r6.claim: This divine attribute is not conjugated like others; only a form transmitted from the Prophet or imams may be used.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p9#2/r6.anchor: لا يقال: أمن الله؛ كما يقال: تقدس الله. ولا يقال: يؤمن الله

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r1.claim: Īmān means affirmation: in Joseph’s story it means believing the brothers, and in 40:12 it means affirming God alone.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r2.claim: A servant is a believer by affirming; God is al-Muʾmin because He confirms His promise or accepts the servant’s faith.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r2.anchor: والعبد مؤمن بالله، أي مصدق. والله مؤمن: مصدق ما وعده، أو قابل إيمانه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r3.claim: In ordinary speech ما أومن بشيء مما تقول means “I do not affirm anything you say.”
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p263/r3.anchor: ويقال في الكلام: ما أومن بشيء مما تقول أي ما أصدق به

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p185/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p185/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p185/r1.claim: The author lists Quranic negative clauses in which ب precedes a predicate, including the brothers’ claim that Jacob would not believe them even if truthful.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p185/r1.anchor: يوسف 17: {وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين}

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r1.claim: Early qirāʾāt argument was scattered and incomplete, first relying on analogy between similar forms or roots before developing fuller grammatical explanation and citation.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r1.anchor: ثم أخذ يتجه مع ذلك إلى التخريج والاستشهاد

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r5.speaker: الكسائي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī is reported to read al-dhīb in 12:17 without hamza, while Ḥamza ibn Ḥabīb gives the hamzated form al-dhiʾb.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r5.anchor: ويروون أن الكسائي قرأ أمام حمزة بن حبيب: "فأكله الذيب"6 بغير همز، فقال حمزة

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r6.speaker: حمزة بن حبيب
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r6.claim: Ḥamza ibn Ḥabīb responds with the hamzated reading of the wolf in contrast to al-Kisāʾī’s unhamzated form.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r7.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r7.speaker: الكسائي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī asks why Hamza marks al-dhiʾb with hamza while leaving al-ḥūt unhamzated, invoking the parallel fish wording; this excerpt ends before Hamza’s answer.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r7.anchor: فقال الكسائي: وكذلك أهمز الحوت "فالتقمه الحؤت"؟ 7 قال: لا

BURHAN:v4p107/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p107/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p107/r1.claim: Sometimes an apparent sequence is a resumption with an omitted question: after the brothers arrive crying, an imagined “what did they say?” is answered by “O our father,” so there is no conjunction.
BURHAN:v4p107/r1.anchor: الحال الرابعة إن يكون بتقدير الاستئناف كأن قائلا قال لم كان كذا فقيل كذا فهاهنا لا عطف أيضا

BURHAN:v2p358/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p358/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p358/r1.claim: The conditional particles لو and لما take past-form verbs, so they are exceptions to the rule that condition verbs have future meaning.
BURHAN:v2p358/r1.anchor: واستدرك عليه لو ولما الشرطيتين فان الفعل بعدهما لايكون الا ماضيا فتعين استثناؤه من قوله لايكون الا مستقبل المعنى

BURHAN:v2p358/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p358/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p358/r9.claim: The brothers mean Jacob would not believe them even if their innocence were manifest, because he favored Joseph; their fabricated evidence and plot exposed their lie.
BURHAN:v2p358/r9.anchor: فالمعنى والله اعلم ما انت بمصدق لنا ولو ظهرت لك براءتنا بتفضيلك اياه علينا وقد اتوه بدلائل كاذبة ولم يصدقهم

BURHAN:v3p454/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p454/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p454/r1.claim: Although مصدق would echo صادقين, مؤمن adds the sense of granting security as well as believing, which better expresses the brothers' request.
BURHAN:v3p454/r1.anchor: والجواب أن في مؤمن لنا من المعنى ما ليس في مصدق وذلك أنك إذا قلت مصدق لي فمعناه قال لي صدقت

ITQAN:v3p246/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p246/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p246/r1.claim: مؤمن لنا says more than مصدق: it combines belief with granting security, fitting the brothers' request for reassurance as well as acceptance of their story.
ITQAN:v3p246/r1.anchor: قال لي صدقت وأما ( مؤمن ) فمعناه

ITQAN:v3p246/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p246/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p246/r2.claim: Semantic force can outweigh wordplay, which is an embellishment of sound rather than meaning; the verse keeps مؤمن لنا despite مصدق's better rhyme.
ITQAN:v3p246/r2.anchor: لكون الجناس من المحاسن اللفظية لا المعنوية
